How McDonald's became a real estate empire. In 2025, McDonald's collected $10.4 billion in rent from franchisees, more than the $9.7 billion of food sold at its own restaurants. This video covers how Ray Kroc and Harry Sonneborn built the landlord model through Franchise Realty Corporation in 1956, where McDonald's $26.9 billion of 2025 revenue came from, a hypothetical rent-and-royalty example ($4 million in sales, 5% royalty, an assumed 10% rent = $600,000), why franchised margins (84.2%) dwarf company-operated margins (14.7%), what McDonald's owns (about 56% of the land and 80% of the buildings in its consolidated markets), and the $8.5 billion franchisee support plan with rent relief announced at its September 23, 2026 Investor Day.
